findings.title: Multiple dependent claims improperly built on other multiple dependent claims (US)
findings.attack: 37 CFR 1.75(c)/MPEP 608.01(n)(iii) bars a multiple dependent claim from being based on another multiple dependent claim; 53 of 102 claims violate this, which a US examiner will object to before reaching the merits.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Restructure claim dependencies so no multiple dependent claim's range includes another; restore any lost combinations as separate claims. No scope lost.

findings.title: Independent claims not in EPO two-part form
findings.attack: Rule 43(1) EPC expects independent claims to be split into a preamble over the closest prior art and a characterising portion; none of the seven independent claims is so drafted, inviting an EPO examiner's recast request.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast into two-part form once the closest prior art is selected at EPO entry; no scope change.

findings.title: Inconsistent reference-sign practice across the claim set
findings.attack: Claims 79-89 omit reference numerals used consistently for the same components in claims 1, 58, 67 and 90-102.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the existing reference numerals to claims 79-89 at first mention.

corrections.from_text: 10. The valve core of any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the deflectable ring element has a wall arranged such that an axial load applied to the deflectable ring element by the poppet in over-travel is converted into the radial deflection.
corrections.to: [No single text substitution cures this claim in isolation; requires claim-set renumbering per F-40a-1/F-37-1.]

corrections.from_text: 67. A seat ring (30) for a valve core of an inflation valve, the seat ring being an annular element having a sealing edge (34) at one axial end of the seat ring for seating a sealing face of a poppet, and a wall between the one axial end and an opposite axial end of the seat ring, the wall comprising a convoluted wall (32) having one or more convolutions, the convoluted wall converting an axial load applied to the seat ring into a radial deflection of the seat ring, the seat ring undergoing shape recovery to its at-rest form on removal of the axial load, and the seat ring having a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm.
corrections.to: 67. A seat ring (30) for a valve core of an inflation valve, the seat ring being an annular element having a sealing edge (34) at one axial end of the seat ring for seating a sealing face of a poppet, and a wall between the one axial end and an opposite axial end of the seat ring, the seat ring having a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm, characterised in that the wall comprises a convoluted wall (32) having one or more convolutions, the convoluted wall converting an axial load applied to the seat ring into a radial deflection of the seat ring, the seat ring undergoing shape recovery to its at-rest form on removal of the axial load.
corrections.reason: Illustrates the Rule 43(1) EPC two-part split; final characterising portion depends on the prior-art document selected at EPO entry.
Resolves reference-sign inconsistency identified in F-40a-3.

assumptions.text: US/EPO/UK assessed per the matter's standing default jurisdictions; no matter.json override supplied.
EPO two-part-form expectation applied per Rule 43(1) EPC/Guidelines F-IV 2.2-2.3; can be dispensed with where inappropriate, a judgment call for EPO counsel.
No physical drawing sheets were supplied; drawing-formality requirements marked not applicable/cannot assess.
Independent/total claim counts used for the informational fee note will change once Correction 1 is implemented.
